html:
Velupillai Prabhakaran was the founder and leader of the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE), the armed group that fought for a Tamil state in northern and eastern Sri Lanka. He was born in 1954 at Valvettithurai, near Jaffna.

Angered by the Sinhala Only Act and attacks on Tamils, he founded the Tigers in 1976 and built them into a disciplined guerrilla army with a navy, suicide squads and a near state in the north. After Black July in 1983 they led the civil war. The Tigers killed the Indian leader Rajiv Gandhi in 1991 and President Ranasinghe Premadasa in 1993.

The army killed Prabhakaran in May 2009 in the last battle of the war, on the northeast coast. The Tigers died with him.
